incident_summary.description: Users are unable to log into the web application following the deployment of version 2.8.1, encountering 500 Internal Server Errors and severe loading delays.
incident_summary.impact: Users cannot log in to the web application, HTTP 500 errors are returned, response times exceed 8 seconds, system resources are heavily loaded (CPU 92%, Memory 89%), and the application health check is unhealthy.

timeline.event: Cache warm-up took longer than expected
Failed to connect to Redis cache
Login request failed for user ID 1023
Login request failed for user ID 2035
Health check endpoint returned unhealthy status

root_causes.title: Redis Connection Failure Leading to Database Resource Exhaustion
root_causes.explanation: Version 2.8.1 introduced Redis-based session caching. When the application failed to connect to Redis, it fell back directly to database queries for session/login management. This sudden shift in traffic exhausted the database connection pool, leading to query timeouts, high response times, high system load, and HTTP 500 failures.

root_causes.title: Redis Network or Configuration Misconfiguration in Release 2.8.1
root_causes.explanation: The newly deployed version 2.8.1 may contain incorrect Redis connection parameters (e.g., host, port, authentication credentials) or the Redis cluster/instance itself is unreachable or offline.

evidence: Deployment notes state version 2.8.1 introduced Redis-based session caching.
Log entry at 10:05:11 records 'Failed to connect to Redis cache'.
Log entry at 10:05:13 records 'Falling back to database queries'.
Log entries at 10:05:48 and 10:31:12 record 'Database connection pool exhausted'.
Log entry at 10:06:27 records 'Timeout while executing SQL query'.
Log entries at 10:06:05 and 10:07:18 confirm HTTP 500 errors were returned to clients.
Log entries at 10:08:02 and 10:08:14 show CPU reaching 92% and Memory reaching 89%.
Log entry at 10:08:31 reports the health check endpoint returned unhealthy status.
assumptions: The Redis connection failure directly caused the excessive load on the database due to the fallback mechanism.
Login authentication depends on reading or writing session data that was intended to be served by Redis.
uncertainties: The exact reason why the connection to Redis failed (e.g., wrong host/port in v2.8.1 config, firewall rule, or down Redis instance).
Whether the database server itself is impaired or simply overwhelmed by connection count and query queueing.
immediate_actions: Verify the Redis server operational status, network connectivity, and authentication settings.
Check the version 2.8.1 configuration files/environment variables for accurate Redis connection details.
If Redis cannot be quickly recovered or reconfigured, rollback deployment version 2.8.1 to the previous stable release.
long_term_actions: Implement rate limiting or circuit breaker patterns on database fallback paths to prevent connection pool exhaustion during cache outages.
Enhance deployment sanity checks to validate connectivity to external services (like Redis) prior to routing live traffic.
Set up specific monitoring and alerting for cache connection failures separate from general application health endpoints.

incident: Users are reporting that they cannot log into the web application after today's deployment. Some users receive a "500 Internal Server Error", while others experience long loading times before the login page fails.
